Subject: Recap & next steps — PII handling for pilot

Thanks for the time earlier today — great conversation. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we're aligned: 

Summary of Acme's asks:
- You want clarity on what Redwood stores from API calls (prompts, generated outputs, embeddings), where that data is stored, retention windows, and logging controls for debugging.
- Data residency requirement: US-only (us-east-1) for the pilot.
- Need SOC 2 summary and a signed DPA for procurement.

High-level commitment from Redwood (for Hosted API pilot):
- By default, request payloads (prompts) and model outputs are logged for up to 30 days to support debugging and abuse detection.
- We provide an opt-out for persistent storage for customer data ("data_retention: no_persist") which prevents prompts/outputs from being stored beyond transient logs used for immediate inference; this is available for pilot customers on request.
- Embeddings are not stored persistently unless explicitly enabled by the customer.
- Logs and stored artifacts for hosted customers are kept in the customer-requested AWS region (we can pin to us-east-1). Data is encrypted at rest using AWS KMS.
- For Dedicated and Private deployments, persistent storage is under customer control; Redwood does not ingest logs for training in those modes.

Attachments I'm including here: SOC2_summary.pdf and a standard DPA draft (DPA_Redwood_v1.docx).

Next steps:
1) I'll loop in Neha (security) for a brief technical call to confirm encryption/key management and logging scope.
2) We'll provide a short matrix that explicitly calls out: prompts stored (Y/N), outputs stored (Y/N), embeddings stored (Y/N), retention windows per artifact, and where data is stored.
3) Procurement: review and sign DPA; I'll follow up with a DocuSign link.

Are you available for a 30-minute technical call on Friday 9/11 morning PT?

Thanks,
Rishi Malhotra
Account Exec — Redwood Inference

Thanks Rishi — helpful recap. A few clarifying questions before we schedule the technical call: 

1) Can you confirm exactly which artifacts are stored by default for the hosted API? Specifically: 
   - Full prompt text (including any PII in prompts)
   - Model outputs
   - Embeddings (if we call the embeddings endpoint)

2) For the 30-day retention you noted: is that retention applied to both prompts and outputs and to any debug logs that include token-level info?

3) If we opt into the "no_persist" mode for the pilot, are there any features that stop working (e.g., rate-limited debugging, customer support access to logs)? Any implications for latency or functionality?

4) For encryption and keys: is Redwood using customer-managed keys (CMK) or Redwood-managed keys by default? We prefer CMK if possible.

5) Please confirm data residency: all stored artifacts must remain in us-east-1 for this pilot; any cross-region backups should be disabled.

Finally — we'll need the SOC2 summary and the DPA to go to procurement. Appreciate if you can send the DocuSign link.

Subject: Re: Recap & next steps — PII handling for pilot

Samantha — thanks for the questions. Below are explicit confirmations and a few notes on trade-offs. Happy to go into detail on the tech call; Neha will lead the security portion.

Quick confirmations (Hosted API):
- Full prompt text: By default we persist prompt payloads for 30 days for debugging and abuse detection. If you require, we can enable the customer opt-out ("no_persist") for the pilot which prevents persistent storage of prompts. In no_persist mode, we still process the request in-memory for inference but do not write prompts to long-term storage.

- Model outputs: Also persisted by default for 30 days. Outputs can be excluded under the same no_persist option.

- Embeddings: Not stored persistently by default unless you opt to enable embedding indexing/storage. Calls to the embeddings endpoint return vectors but we do not index or store them unless configured.

- Token-level debug logs: We retain minimal transient logs for immediate processing. If you require, we can turn off token-level detailed logs for the pilot; doing so will reduce our ability to debug fine-grained inference issues but does not affect real-time latency.

Retention & region:
- Default retention: 30 days for prompts/outputs.
- Region: We can pin both transient and persistent storage to us-east-1 for the pilot; cross-region backups will be disabled.

Encryption & keys:
- Default: Redwood-managed KMS keys (AWS KMS) for hosted customers.
- Enterprise option: customer-managed keys (CMK) are available as an enterprise control (we'll surface the CMK option in the DPA/contract).

Dedicated/Private options:
- If you prefer to avoid any hosted persistence, Dedicated or Private deployment places storage and keys under your control and Redwood does not ingest customer data for training or analytics in those modes.

Support & functionality trade-offs for no_persist:
- No change to model latency or core inference functionality.
- Reduced post-hoc debugging capability; we'll rely on live support and session-level telemetry that does not persist full content.

Attachments & links:
- SOC2_summary.pdf (attached) — 1-page summary of current SOC 2 status and scope.
- DPA_Redwood_v1.docx (attached) — standard DPA; we've prepared a DocuSign envelope for easy signing: https://docusign.com/embedded/ABC12345

Next steps:
1) Can you confirm whether you want us to enable no_persist for the pilot?
2) I'll schedule a 30-min technical call with Neha; propose Fri 9/11 9:30 AM PT / 12:30 PM ET.
3) I will open the DocuSign envelope to your procurement team; please let me know the signee.

Thanks — copying Neha for the technical/crypto details.
